title: Authorization, tenancy, field-level access
status: AUTHORED. Technique layer lives in web-attack-atlas W02 (50 gated patterns). This document is the tooling and the decision path.

atom_notes.A02: the core primitive: a lower principal borrows higher authority
atom_notes.A03: identity confusion makes the authorisation decision use the wrong subject
atom_notes.A05: shape confusion lets a value pass validation and mean something else when written
atom_notes.A06: path and namespace confusion makes the route authorise a different object than the handler uses

required_cells.why: object inventory and ownership mapping before any test
enumerate ids, roles and tenants systematically
prove the write lands on another principal's object
negative control that the same request fails for a third identity
impact framing, or the finding closes as informational
retest after the fix, replaying the exact request
continuous drift detection on role and scope changes

entries.name: Row level security reasoning (Postgres/Supabase class)
entries.role: When authorisation lives in the database, the test is an RLS bypass class, not an endpoint check
preconditions: authorisation delegated to row level policies
client talks to the database directly
oracle: row visible that the policy should hide
entries.note: Common in modern stacks and almost never in authz test checklists, because the test surface is the client SDK not an HTTP endpoint.

tree.q: Does the application authorise on objects (BOLA) or on functions (BFLA) or both?
tree.why: The test procedure diverges completely. BOLA needs two identities and object ids. BFLA needs a role matrix.

next.q: Do you have two accounts at different privilege levels and at least one object owned by a third?

branches.action: run the same request set as both identities, diff responses, then substitute ids across owners

next.q: Does the difference survive a third identity and a negative control?
next.action: third identity must be denied; a nonexistent id must 404. Otherwise it is an artifact

branches.action: create them. authz cannot be tested with one identity, and this is the most common reason it is not tested

branches.a: Authorisation is in the database (RLS, policies)
branches.action: test the client SDK path directly, not the HTTP API. look for policies that reference a user supplied claim
branches.oracle: row visible that policy should hide

branches.a: Authorisation is in a gateway or policy engine
branches.action: test the gateway and the service independently. the gap between them is the finding surface
branches.oracle: same request, different decision at two layers

gaps.gap: No tool automatically creates N identities and replays a full captured session as each
gaps.build_candidate: given a HAR and N credentials, replay every request N times and emit the access matrix as JSON

gaps.gap: No tool diffs gateway decisions against service decisions for the same request
gaps.build_candidate: dual-send the request to both layers and compare status plus body hash

gaps.gap: No credible RLS/policy tester that works from the client SDK rather than the REST layer
gaps.build_candidate: wrap the client SDK, enumerate tables via the API surface, probe row visibility per identity
